title: Meta Funds Seven Gas Plants to Power Biggest Data Center
key_facts: Meta is paying for seven new natural gas plants to supply its Hyperion campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, under a new agreement with Entergy, announced on a Friday (27 Mar 2026).
The plants add 5.2 GW; three plants approved in 2025 add about 2.3 GW; total 10 gas facilities and more than 7 GW.
The seven new plants still need regulators' sign-off before construction.
Meta will also fund 240 miles of new transmission lines, battery storage and nuclear power uprates at existing Entergy facilities.
Entergy says Meta 'pays its full cost of service' and projects more than $2 billion in customer savings over 20 years.
Meta declined to say how much it will spend; about 5 GW of the campus draw goes to compute.
quote_evidence: Meta is paying for the construction of seven new natural gas plants to supply its largest data center, massively expanding the fossil fuel infrastructure underpinning its AI buildout.
Still, the seven new plants will need their own sign-off from state regulators before construction can begin.
Meta declined to say how much it would spend on the gas plants and associated infrastructure, per Bloomberg.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how far a single AI campus can reshape a regional grid.
notes: Old news re-dated into the 8 Oct window by the feed (EnergyNow republication). Later coverage (NOLA.com 8 Oct) concerns Entergy's regulatory hearing.
